name: A child's life threatened, and delivered
description: A child's death seems certain — by the knife, by thirst in the wilderness, by royal decree — and God provides a way through at the last possible moment.

name: Famine drives them to a foreign land
description: Famine in the promised land sends God's people to sojourn among foreigners — and, generations later, home again.

name: "I am with you"
description: At a moment of fear or a fresh commission, God speaks the same reassurance — his presence, not a removal of the danger, is the answer given.

name: Standing in the gap for others
description: Someone pleads with God on behalf of people who have no claim on mercy of their own — Abraham bargaining for Sodom, Moses offering himself in place of a people who had just betrayed him.

name: Meeting a spouse at a well
description: A future wife is found at a well, in a foreign land, through an act of hospitality or defense — Isaac's, Jacob's, and Moses's wives are all met exactly this way.

name: The deceiver deceived
description: Jacob takes his brother's blessing in disguise, using animal skins to fool his father's touch. He is deceived in turn by Laban, married to the wrong sister in the dark. His own sons then deceive him with an animal's blood on his favorite son's coat.

name: Presuming on what is holy
description: Approaching what God has set apart, or the role he assigned someone else, without his authorization — with immediate and severe consequence.

name: Grumbling in the wilderness
description: Complaints about food, water, or the journey bring either God’s provision or his judgment — sometimes both in the same story.

name: The younger son is chosen
description: God repeatedly bypasses the culturally expected right of the firstborn: Isaac over Ishmael, Jacob over Esau, Joseph exalted above his ten older brothers.
